title: Severe allergic reactions (anaphylaxis)
description: A severe, rapid allergic reaction that can affect breathing and circulation. Triggers include food (peanuts, shellfish), insect stings, and medications.

recognition_questions.q: Is there swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat?
Is the person having difficulty breathing, wheezing, or feeling faint?
Is there a widespread rash, hives, or flushed skin?

observable_symptoms: Swelling of lips, tongue, throat, or face
immediate_safety_warnings: Anaphylaxis can kill within minutes — act immediately.
If the person has an adrenaline auto-injector (EpiPen), help them use it without delay.

ordered_instructions.rationale: Anaphylaxis is life-threatening and can recur.

ordered_instructions.instruction: If the person has an adrenaline auto-injector, help them use it on the outer thigh (through clothing if needed). Note the time.
Help the person sit up if they have difficulty breathing, or lie them flat with legs raised if they feel faint.
ordered_instructions.rationale: Position affects breathing and blood pressure.

ordered_instructions.instruction: If no improvement in 5 minutes and a second auto-injector is available, give a second dose.
ordered_instructions.rationale: Anaphylaxis can recur or not respond.

ordered_instructions.instruction: If the person becomes unconscious but breathing, place in recovery position. If not breathing, start CPR.

actions_to_avoid: Do not let the person stand or walk — it can cause a sudden fatal drop in blood pressure.
Do not give any medication by mouth if the person is having difficulty breathing or is drowsy.
Do not assume the reaction is over once adrenaline is given — it can recur.

escalation_conditions.condition: Any swelling of throat/tongue, wheeze, or collapse after a trigger
escalation_conditions.action: Call 112; use adrenaline auto-injector if available

escalation_conditions.condition: Symptoms not improving after first adrenaline dose
escalation_conditions.action: Give second dose if available; ensure 112 called

escalation_conditions.condition: Person becomes unconscious and stops breathing

equipment_requirements.item: Adrenaline auto-injector (if the person has one)

follow_up_requirements: All anaphylaxis requires hospital observation for at least 6 hours (biphasic reaction risk).
Refer for an allergy assessment and an action plan.

age_specific_pathways.child: Use the child-dose auto-injector if available; same technique.
age_specific_pathways.infant: Urgent care; auto-injector dosing per age/weight as prescribed.

source_references.document: International First Aid, Resuscitation and Education Guidelines
